title: Real-terrain tiles under shifted physics
status: pre-registered before any method was run on real tiles with shifted physics
purpose: A2 found that on real-terrain tiles (ID physics) the assured system ties A* on success with far fewer unsafe moves. A4 tests whether this holds under the sensor and dynamics shifts where A* won on procedural maps.
tiles: the frozen A2 real_final tile set (data/real_tiles/hirise_tiles.npz, sha256 3a44de6ef624ca1d1804e3ce931bd6052967e4dba21dd08a58bc60a32d2b519c), 450 tiles, seeds 70000-70449

conditions.real_combined: configs/sim32_real_combined.yaml = sensor + dynamics shift physics of configs/sim32_combined_shift.yaml (its terrain component does not apply: terrain is the real tile)

note_terrain_shift: no terrain-shift condition: on real tiles the terrain is fixed by the DTM
statistics: as v1.1: paired by system seed on identical tiles (seedless A* paired with every seed), 95% t interval, exact sign-flip p, Holm across the three conditions within each (comparison, metric); alpha 0.05
key_question: Does 'assured vs A*' success remain non-significantly different (as on real terrain with ID physics), or does A* regain a significant success advantage under shifted physics? Reported as found; no decision threshold beyond the significance tests.
reproduction_check: the v1.1 cell assured@95 / seed 0 / id must be byte-identical when re-run from the amended code
